newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks faces strike threat in Vancouver.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks faces strike threat in Vancouver.

text.p: Contract negotiations between Starbucks Corp and unionized workers in British Columbia were stalled ahead of a Thursday strike deadline, officials said.
"The talks are pretty well stalled on both sides," a Vancouver spokeswoman for the coffee-bar chain said.

The Canadian Auto Workers union presented the company with a new contract proposal late last week but Seattle-based Starbucks rejected it. "In Starbucks mind, there were no substantive changes," the spokeswoman said.

The union, which represents about 110 workers at eight retail locations and a distribution center, is trying to negotiate the first union contract at Starbucks which has more than 1,000 outlets in North America.
Union officials were not available for comment, but one union representative told the Vancouver Sun newspaper that job action loomed.

"Obviously we're headed towards some type of job action," CAW official John Bowman told the newspaper. "They haven't offered to meet and they haven't offered to give a monetary position. In our view they're continuing to stall and avoid making a serious effort to negotiate.

The Starbucks spokeswoman said the union could choose to hold off on a strike. If it does go on strike, the company believes the walkout could not begin until Friday because the union must first apply to the provincial labor board to be released from mediation.
The main issues in the negotiations are work flexibility issues such as scheduling and wages. The union is demanding a starting wage of C$10 an hour compared to C$7 currently.
